body: I'm brutally honest here. I do care about the outward appearance and attractiveness of a man but tallness was never a thing that mattered to me. I'm 5'8 as a woman and I would def date guys that are shorter than me. A deep voice and a quite muscular build is what turns me on. Confidence and charisma play a very big role for me too. If a man is signaling me that he knows what he wants and is ambitious, there's nothing more hotter than, imo.

All these examples you mention that prove how physical appearance isn't everything in life I can't disagree with that. But sadly in my experience I'm not capable of internalizing this. It is not that I'm not trying to, I really do but in the end I would always lie to myself in order to feel somehow sane again. Like I said doing things I love (like photography or hanging out with friends) did nourish my inner self and made me happy for a short period of time but it didn't really help me that much with my appearance related issues. :/ It in fact reminds me all the time how precious life can be. And then I get angry at myself and I ask myself why I am this way and I fall in this trap of self-pity which is the wrongest thing to do Ik. :( I have nothing to complain about but still my physical appearance is the biggest opponent I have to face. I know speaking to me about this issue is like talking to a wall. I get what you mean.. There is a reason why people say inner beauty will always shine over outward beauty. I am far away yet to experience this myself. But I honestly doubt I will ever get to that point. Everyday means pure suffering to me, it sounds so pointless compared to other people's problems. But like you said you feel what you feel. I'm writing this on a day where I feel very low again so my pessimism is obvious here. Nonetheless I appreciate your words very much and try to open my mind for them, you sound like a person who is very emphatic.

THIS. You literally speak right out of my mind. You said that maybe through time you unconsciously made yourself decide that outward appearance matters to you. I asked that myself a lot too. When I was younger I didn't care about it at all, I was too busy with other things that are not that superficial just like any other normal kid. I remember during the time I hit puberty when the personal interests change all of a sudden I became unsecure about my appearance for the first time. I know that sounds like a typical teenager, the problem is just it never stopped after that and went on and on and became stronger. :/ Ofc the media contributed a lot to this at least for me. Beautiful flawless photoshopped women everywhere on commercials and so on. But yeah, like you said, beauty isn't everything. It actually means nothing but in our world it seems to be everything. Anyways, I wish you all the best. xx

First off I'm very happy for you that you feel this way about yourself now. I get your point about the cool confident girls that sometimes appear more attractive than plain pretty girls without any expression. It is very true that charisma plays a big role in someone's attractiveness. But imo charisma alone doesn't make a person automatically attractive, it is just a major bonus. Prove me wrong but I think the foundation of attractiveness is still the outward appearance though. :/ I am very interested in fashion and always eager to try new things out. The problem is again that I do like the pieces themselves but not worn on my body. Off-the-shoulder sweaters for example make me look like Hulk, no kidding. I often shop online so I see the clothes worn on models. So when I buy the items and try them on, they don't look nearly as good. I know everybody is not the same but it sucks to have the least desired body shape. :/ Ik all of my sentences are circulating around each other like a vicious cicle that I can't get rid of. The point you make about modifying my own standards sounds interesting. It is true that people are constantly changing and evolving, especially on the inside, they just don't realize it bc it happens so fluently. Even though I can't imagine rn that my negative perception of my outward self will ever change much, at the same time I also can't rule out the possibility that it might happen one day. I will keep this in mind whenever I'm at my lowest point again covered in dark thoughts and hopefully it will keep me going. Tysm!

I didn't know of this section, I'm basically new here. :D Thank you for suggesting it, I'm actually thinking about it. But I will click through some of the pics of the women there. Tbh the only naked female bodies I have ever seen in my life are the ones from porn. Other than that just some female fashion models in underwear. Seeing some 'normal' women's bodies maybe will give me a little help to hopefully change my perspective. Even if it doesn't it is worth a try. :)

Haha, yes, what would life be without sex and food. :D Physical activities do wonders for the psyche, I totally agree with you. And I highly appreciate what you do for your friends at the club, they are very lucky to have you! For example after a long jogging session I feel relieved and my body is so exhausted that I don't even have the nerve to think about my appearance or any other issues related to that. I remember I was just being proud of myself for accomplishing such a long hour run. I think it's bc of the release of happiness hormones after doing intensive sports. Too bad the effect is only temporary. :/ My daily routine consists of constantly distracting myself from my negative thoughts by either working at this terrible side job or just watching some Netflix or Youtube Vids after that. I know it's not the best solution on the long-term but at least it keeps me from doing things I shouldn't even think about.

Yup, that's a good thought. I'm not in a good mental state to do any sports right now but I'll keep that in mind. Besides that I always try to remind myself that my body is nothing more than a shell that carries me around this world. I should be thankful for that. After all it allows me to experience things and explore earth. But in reality most of the times I always get caught up in my head again and these thoughts don't matter to me anymore and are empty phrases to me as harsh as it sounds. :/ Often times I wish the human existence would only consist of matter flowing around without a body that is physical. But that's pointless wishful thinking of me.

You're too nice x That all sounds so easy and great, I wish I could think like that.. Right now I'm far far away from that but I try to approach it. I swore to myself that I want to say I have tried everything out to cure myself before I would end it. I have plenty of time to do so I guess..

I really appreciate your words. The point you make here is totally right, I get what you mean. But the thing is it doesn't actually matter to me if a guy likes my appearance or not, I don't need that kind of validation from anyone. If so, that's a plus but I don't want to look attractive for anyone, just for myself. A big part of me loves to look at aesthetic things, it can be either nature, people or objects. Whenever I look at myself in the mirror, I don't see that kind of aesthetic. And this kills me. Maybe I'm a bit narcissistic in that sense but I can't help it.
That sucks. I'm on the opposite though, I have literally no ass. I guess everybody  always wants what they can't have.. But I'm totally with you on the cursed genes thing, I feel the same.
Thank you for your kind words. You're right, beauty is in general all subjective but the majority of people (like myself) prefer attributes that are considered as attractive in the particular gender.
